architectural_risks: Coarse-grained service boundary: owner-pet-service holds multiple subdomains (owners, pets, visits), potentially leading to high internal complexity.
Tight entity coupling: bidirectional references between Owner, Pet, and Visit make any future finer-grained separation difficult without substantial domain model refactoring.
critique: The structural call graph exhibits two distinct connected components with zero cross-module call edges or repository accesses between org.springframework.samples.petclinic.vet and org.springframework.samples.petclinic.owner. Decomposing the monolith into vet-service and owner-pet-service cleanly aligns with physical module boundaries and dependency cuts. While a separate visits service is a common domain concept, the evidence shows that VisitController relies directly on OwnerRepository and domain classes share static references, which would induce distributed transaction overhead and tight inter-service coupling if split without prior refactoring.

migration_priority.reason: Completely disconnected from other components in static calls and data relations; can be extracted first with zero coupling risk to the rest of the application.
Forms the core domain cluster with tightly interconnected data access and static references; represents the remaining monolith core after vet extraction.
